paths.description: First-visit regional consent journey; verifies equal reject/accept choice and handoff to the app.
Public text-translation SPA; represents core task and shared shell for Text, Images, Documents, and Websites modes.
Not covered: signed-in History/Saved data, Google Accounts, file upload contents, and exhaustive language combinations because they require credentials/private files or share the audited shell.

findings.summary: The app does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: Raw-CDP preference probe reports prefers-color-scheme: dark=true while body remains rgb(255,255,255), text remains dark, and computed color-scheme is normal. The dark-condition screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and make the existing theme selection default to the system preference, while preserving the manual override.

findings.summary: Major state and document changes are abrupt rather than continuity-preserving.
findings.evidence: The consent-to-app video shows an instant document swap, and app CSS inspection found no view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for the consent handoff and same-document transitions for major translation-mode changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Overlay-triggering controls are present without CSS anchor-positioning support.
findings.evidence: The app exposes language pickers, Settings, and menus, while live stylesheet inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and pickers that must remain attached near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Rich overlays are implemented without the platform dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered app contains Settings and picker surfaces, but DOM inspection found zero dialog elements and zero popover attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient pickers and settings surfaces to popover or dialog as appropriate, retaining accessible focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Lab LCP narrowly misses the good threshold during the first-use consent-to-app journey.
findings.evidence: The DevTools trace summary measured LCP at 2616.89 ms. CLS was 0 and total blocking time was only 11 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element and shorten its discovery and delivery path, including the consent return path, to provide margin below 2.5 seconds.

findings.summary: The first-use journey transfers a large script-led payload and retains parser-priority blocking candidates.
findings.evidence: HAR summary records 1,590,577 transferred bytes, including 991,384 script bytes and 207,052 font bytes. It identifies a VeryHigh-priority parser stylesheet and High-priority parser scripts; DOM inspection confirms loaded external scripts are not async, defer, or modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the critical script/font chain, defer noncritical modules, and load translation modes and supporting UI only when requested.

findings.summary: JavaScript and same-organization third-party delivery dominate page weight.
findings.evidence: 24 script requests transfer 991,384 bytes; 55 requests and 1,312,350 bytes are outside translate.google.com, led by 1,013,713 bytes from www.gstatic.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Run code coverage on each translation mode, split dormant modes and panels, and remove or delay modules not needed for text translation.

findings.summary: The primary translator contains invalid ARIA and an unnamed input-tools button.
findings.evidence: axe reports a serious aria-command-name violation on .ita-kd-icon-button and an aria-allowed-role violation because role=combobox is applied to the source textarea.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the input-tools control an accessible name and use a valid combobox structure or remove the invalid textarea role while preserving autocomplete semantics.

findings.summary: Core translator content is poorly represented without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability capture found only 19% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML; title and h1 were absent from raw content, and crawler/browser captures materially differ.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the tool title, purpose, language selectors, and a useful no-JS fallback or explanation so core meaning and next steps survive script failure.

findings.summary: The observed response policy leaves defense-in-depth gaps.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS or Referrer-Policy on the consent response and reported unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval in its combined CSP policy; direct app HEAD also lacked HSTS and Referrer-Policy, though it used nonces, Trusted Types, X-Frame-Options, and nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Send HSTS and an explicit Referrer-Policy consistently, and continue reducing CSP allowances so unsafe-inline/eval are not required on any journey surface.

findings.summary: The app advertises a manifest but has no active service worker or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The live app probe found a web app manifest but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration() returned null.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker and provide a clear offline fallback for the translator shell and recent language configuration.

findings.summary: Inactive translation modes load hidden decorative assets during the text-only journey.
findings.evidence: The app DOM contains both light and dark drag-and-drop PNGs for dormant document/image surfaces, and HAR records these assets before those modes are opened.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load mode-specific imagery only when Documents or Images is selected, and avoid fetching both theme variants eagerly.

taskList.title: Repair primary translator ARIA names and roles
Server-render meaningful translator content and add a no-JS fallback
Reduce and defer the critical JavaScript/font payload
Honor system color scheme by default
Strengthen transport and browser policy headers
Add an offline fallback and service worker
Adopt semantic popover/dialog and anchored overlay positioning
